v.why: With the 0->2 edge removed, node 2 carries less input, so a 3x3 conv on 2->3 has less to transform and gains less.
If edge 0 is none, node 1 receives no signal, so a conv on 1->3 processes nothing and adds almost no accuracy.
With node 1 disconnected from the input, a conv on 1->2 carries no signal, so the edit gains little.
When 2->3 is removed, the direct identity route is a larger share of what reaches the output, so adding it matters more.
Adding a conv to an empty 0->3 edge creates a new input-to-output route, which gains more than replacing an op that already carries a route.
Turning on the otherwise absent 2->3 edge with a conv connects the deeper nodes to the output, which gains more than swapping one existing op for another.
Replacing none with a conv on 0->2 adds a whole new learned path, a larger gain than upgrading an existing op.
Edge 0 gates node 1 and every route through it, so turning it on with a conv unlocks the deeper paths from edges 2 and 4.
A strong 2->3 conv already feeds node 3, so a 1->3 identity route adds mostly redundant signal.
With 1->3 removed, the direct skip is one of fewer routes into node 3 and contributes more.
A 3x3 conv after an upstream pooling edge stacks two spatial smoothers, which oversmooths the features.
A pooled direct route adds blur next to an already rich 2->3 conv, so it is redundant and slightly harmful.
Removing the direct route hurts more when the remaining 1->3 route is only a weak pooling edge.
An upstream skip leaves node 1 as a raw copy of the input, so a 3x3 conv on 1->3 largely duplicates what other routes from node 0 provide.
If 2->3 is none, node 2 cannot reach the output, so removing edge 1 costs nothing and is less harmful than elsewhere.
A conv feeding node 2 is wasted when 2->3 is none and node 2 never reaches the output.
The edge 0 conv pays off through node 1's outgoing routes, so it helps less when 1->3 is removed and only edge 2 remains.
With 2->3 also removed, the direct edge and 1->3 are the only routes to the output, so deleting edge 3 is much more damaging.
A 1x1 conv on 1->3 gains little when node 1 receives no input because edge 0 is none.
With edge 1 removed, node 2 gets features only through the 1->2 route, so a 1x1 conv on 2->3 has less to mix.
